messages:
lucas: Build fail on docs deploy: Docusaurus linkcheck reports duplicate anchor for /guides/migration-v2.

lucas: Error snippet: "DuplicateFragmentError: found duplicate fragment 'upgrade' in page /guides/migration-v2"

priya: Did someone copy a heading from the old migration guide? Duplicate headings often create the same slug.

ana: I dug in: pages/guides/migration-v2.mdx has a fenced code block containing a markdown heading that the MDX parser is treating as a rendered heading when the example is unescaped. Example:

```md
### Upgrade
```

ana: Because the code fence uses ```md, Docusaurus MDX compiled it as real heading in the page tree, producing a second `upgrade` anchor.

priya: Oh yikes. We should use a language-neutral fenced block or escape the hashes in examples. Two quick fixes: change ```md to ```bash or wrap the example in a literal block with indentation.

lucas: I'll open a tiny PR to change the fence languages to `text` and add a note to CONTRIBUTING about not using `md` for fenced examples that contain headings.

docs-bot: @lucas opened PR #3429 — "docs: avoid md fences with raw headings in migration guide" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3429

ci-bot: docs CI started for PR #3429 (docusaurus build + linkcheck)

ci-bot: docusaurus build ✅ for PR #3429 — duplicate fragment fixed

priya: Can we add a small doc-test that checks for fenced codeblocks declared as `md` containing leading `#`? A grep in CI should catch this.

lucas: Good idea, filing follow-up issue #141 to add that lint.

ana: Merged and deployed to staging — anchors look good and deep links resolved. Closing thread. :)
